et \(h\) be the height of tree PQ and breadth of river PS be \(x \mathrm{~ft}\). Angle of elevation subtended by a tree is \(60^{\circ}\). Also, when he retreats 20 feet, the angle becomes \(30^{\circ}\).

\log A+(p-1) \log R & p & 1 \\
\log A+(q-1) \log R & q & 1 \\
\log A+(r-1) \log R & r & 1
\end{array}\right|\)
Split into two determinants and in the first take \(\log A\) common and in the second take \(\log \mathrm{R}\) common
\(\Delta=\log A\left|\begin{array}{lll}
1 & p & 1 \\
1 & q & 1 \\
1 & r & 1
\end{array}\right|+\log R\left|\begin{array}{lll}
p-1 & p & 1 \\
q-1 & q & 1 \\
r-1 & r & 1
\end{array}\right|\)
Apply \(\mathrm{C}_1 \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_3\) in the second

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cyclic process is shown in the p-T diagram. Which of the curves show the same process on a $\mathrm{P}$ - $\mathrm{V}$ diagram?
questions.solution:
- Given diagram: P-T graph.
- Using ideal gas law: \(P V=n R T \Rightarrow V=\frac{n R T}{P}\).
So in a \(P-T\) graph we can infer how \(V\) behaves.
Step analysis of cycle \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{A}\) :
- A \(\rightarrow \mathrm{B}\) : Both \(P\) and \(T\) increase proportionally (straight line through origin).
\(\Rightarrow V=\frac{n R T}{P}=\text { constant. }\)
So \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}\) is an isochoric process in \(P-V\).
- \(\mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}: T\) constant, \(P\) decreases.
\(\Rightarrow\) Isothermal expansion in \(P-V\).
- \(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{A}: P\) constant, \(T\) decreases.
\(\Rightarrow\) Isochoric process in \(P-V\).
So the cycle consists of:
- Isochoric line,
- Isothermal curve,
- Isochoric line.
This matches diagram (2).

questions.q: Two tuning forks $A$ and $B$ sounded together give 6 beats per second. With an air resonance tube closed at one end, the two forks give resonance when the two air columns are $24 \mathrm{~cm}$ and 25 $\mathrm{cm}$ respectively. Calculate the frequencies of forks.
questions.solution:
Let the frequency of the first fork be $\mathrm{f}_{1}$ and that of second be $\mathrm{f}_{2}$
We then have, $\mathrm{f}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \times 24}$ and $\mathrm{f}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \times 25}$
We also see that $\mathrm{f}_{1} \gt \mathrm{f}_{2}$
\therefore \mathrm{f}_{1}-\mathrm{f}_{2}=6

and $\frac{\mathrm{f}_{1}}{\mathrm{f}_{2}}=\frac{24}{25}$
Solving (i) and (ii), we get $\mathrm{f}_{1}=150 \mathrm{~Hz}$ and $\quad \mathrm{f}_{2}=144 \mathrm{~Hz}$
